unconventional gas development means any activity involving unconventional gas production that has, or is likely to have, a significant impact on water resources (including any impacts of associated salt production and/or salinity):

In this Part:
commencement day means the day this Schedule commences.
main Act means the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999.
transitional period means the period of 90 business days (measured in Canberra), beginning on the first such business day that is on or after the commencement day.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Amendments apply to actions taken after commencement

content.p: The amendments made by Part 1 of this Schedule apply in relation to an action involving unconventional gas development that is taken on or after the commencement day, even if the action began before that time, unless item 26, 27 or 28 of this Schedule applies in relation to the action.
If:
a proposal by a person to take the action was referred to the Minister under Division 1 of Part 7 of the main Act before the commencement day; and
immediately before the commencement day, the Minister has not decided whether the action is a controlled action; and
the Minister has given a notice under section 74 of the main Act in relation to the action;
the validity of the notice is not affected by the amendments and the Minister is not required to give another notice under that section.

However, if, after the commencement day, the Minister receives comments in response to the invitation in the notice (and within the period specified in the notice) that relate to whether the action is a controlled action for the purposes of a provision of section 24D or 24E of the main Act as amended by Part 1 of this Schedule, the Minister’s duty under subsection 75(1A) of the main Act to consider comments includes a duty to consider any such comments.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Amendments do not apply—certain referred proposals

content.p: The amendments made by Part 1 of this Schedule do not apply in relation to an action taken on or after the commencement day if, immediately before the commencement day:
an approval of the taking of the action is in operation under Part 9 of the main Act; or
both:
a decision that the action is not a controlled action is in operation under section 75 of the main Act; and
the decision was not made because the Minister believed the action would be taken in a particular manner.
The amendments made by Part 1 of this Schedule do not apply in relation to an action taken on or after the commencement day if:
immediately before that day, a decision that the action is not a controlled action is in operation under section 75 of the main Act; and
the decision was made because the Minister believed the action would be taken in a particular manner; and
the action is being taken in that manner.
The amendments made by Part 1 of this Schedule do not apply in relation to an action taken on or after the commencement day if:
a proposal by a person to take the action was referred to the Minister under Division 1 of Part 7 of the main Act before the commencement day; and
immediately before the commencement day, all of the following circumstances exist:
the Minister has not decided whether or not to approve the taking of the action for the purposes of any controlling provisions;
the person has been informed under section 131AA of the main Act of the decision the Minister proposes to make in relation to the action;

if section 131AB of the main Act applies—the Minister has obtained advice from the Independent Scientific Committee on Coal Seam Gas and Large Coal Mining Development in accordance with subsection 131AB(2) of the main Act.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Amendments do not apply—development currently in production

content.p: The amendments made by Part 1 of this Schedule do not apply in relation to an action involving unconventional gas development taken on or after the commencement day if:
the unconventional gas development does not involve the extraction of coal seam gas; and
the unconventional gas development was in production (within the meaning of subitem (2)) before the commencement day; and
immediately before the commencement day:
the action was authorised by a petroleum production authorisation (within the meaning of subitem (3)); and
the action was not contravening a provision of Part 3 of the main Act; and
the action continues to be authorised by the petroleum production authorisation.
(2) For the purposes of this item, a development is in production if the development is extracting or producing gas:
commercially; and
in accordance with the laws of the Commonwealth and of any State or Territory that apply in relation to the development.

(3) For the purposes of this item, a petroleum production authorisation is a licence, permit, or other authority granted under a law of the Commonwealth or a State or Territory, that authorises the extraction of petroleum for commercial production. However, it does not include a lease or licence that is primarily for the purpose of reservation, retention or exploration.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Amendments do not apply—development that has ceased operation

content.p: The amendments made by Part 1 of this Schedule do not apply in relation to an action involving unconventional gas development taken on or after the commencement day if:
the unconventional gas development does not involve the extraction of coal seam gas; and
immediately before the commencement day, the action was not contravening a provision of Part 3 of the main Act; and
immediately before the commencement day, either or both of the following apply:
extraction and production of gas by the development had permanently ceased;
post-production had permanently ceased.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Minister to decide whether amended provisions are controlling provisions for certain controlled actions

content.p: This item applies in relation to an action if:
a proposal by a person to take the action was referred to the Minister under Division 1 of Part 7 of the main Act before the commencement day; and
the action involves unconventional gas development; and
item 26 does not apply in relation to the action; and
before the commencement day, the Minister decided under section 75 of the main Act that the action is a controlled action; and
immediately before the commencement day, the Minister has not decided whether or not to approve the taking of action under Part 9 of the main Act.

The Minister must, before the end of the transitional period, decide in accordance with this item whether any provisions of section 24D or 24E of the main Act as amended by Part 1 of this Schedule are controlling provisions for the action.
Before making the decision, the Minister must give the person proposing to take the action a written notice:
setting out the decision the Minister proposes to make; and
inviting the person to give the Minister written comments on the proposed decision within 10 business days (measured in Canberra) of the day the notice is given to the person.
(4) Before making the decision, the Minister (the Environment Minister) may:
notify any other Minister whom the Environment Minister considers has administrative responsibilities relating to the proposed decision; and
invite the relevant Minister to give the Environment Minister written comments on the proposed decision, within 10 business days (measured in Canberra).

If the Minister believes on reasonable grounds that the Minister does not have enough information to make a decision under subitem (2), the Minister may request the person proposing to take the action to provide specified information relevant to making the decision.

If the Minister requests further information under subitem (5), the period within which the Minister is required to make a decision under subitem (2) is extended by the number of business days in the period:
starting on the day the Minister requests the information; and
ending on the day the Minister receives the last of the information requested.
In making a decision under subitem (2), the Minister must consider:
any comments received within the period specified in an invitation given under paragraph (3)(b) or (4)(b); and
any further information provided in response to a request made under subitem (5); and
any information included in the referral of the proposal to take the action relating to whether the action is a controlled action; and

any other information, or any comments, relating to whether the action is a controlled action received (whether before or after the commencement day) in response to an invitation made before the commencement day under section 74 of the main Act.
Subsections 75(2), (2A) and (2B) of the main Act apply in relation to the Minister’s decision under this item:
as if it were a decision under that section; and
as if references to matters protected by provisions of Part 3 were references to matters protected by provisions of sections 24D and 24E of the main Act as amended by Part 1 of this Schedule.
Within 10 business days after making a decision under subitem (2), the Minister must:
give written notice of the decision to the person proposing to take the action; and
publish notice of the decision in accordance with any regulations made for the purposes of paragraph 77(1)(b) of the main Act.

The Minister must give reasons for the decision to the person proposing to take the action if the person makes a written request, within 28 days of being given the notice, that the Minister do so. The Minister must do so as soon as practicable, and in any case, within 28 days of receiving the request.

(11) The main Act has effect, after the Minister makes a decision under subitem (2) (the new controlling provisions decision), as if the decision mentioned in paragraph (1)(d) (the original controlling provisions decision) were varied to give effect to the new controlling provisions decision.
The validity of the original controlling provisions decision, and any other decision made under Part 7, 8 or 9 of the main Act before the Minister made the new controlling provisions decision:
is not affected by the making of the new controlling provisions decision; and
cannot be revoked, varied, suspended, challenged, reviewed, set aside or called in question because of, or for reasons relating to:
the making of the new controlling provisions decision; or
the variation of the original controlling provisions decision as described in subitem (11).

Anything done by the Minister under this item is not invalid merely because it was not done within the period required by this item. However, this does not reduce or remove an obligation under this item to do a thing within a particular period.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Minister to consider whether assessment approach should be changed

content.p: This item applies in relation to an action if:

(a) the Minister has decided under subitem 29(2) that provisions of sections 24D and 24E of the main Act as amended by Part 1 of this Schedule are controlling provisions for the action (the new controlling provisions decision); and
before the commencement day, the Minister had made a decision under section 87 of the main Act as to the approach to be used for assessment of the relevant impacts of the action.

The Minister may, before the end of the period within which the Minister is required to make the new controlling provisions decision, decide whether, as a result of the new controlling provisions decision, a different approach should be used for assessment of the relevant impacts of the action.

If the Minister believes on reasonable grounds that the Minister does not have enough information to make a decision under subitem (2), the Minister may request the person proposing to take the action to provide specified information relevant to making the decision.

If the Minister requests further information under subitem (3), the period within which the Minister is required to make a decision under subitem (2) is extended by the number of business days in the period:
starting on the day the Minister requests the information; and
ending on the day the Minister receives the last of the information requested.
In making a decision under subitem (2), the Minister must consider:
any further information provided in response to a request made under subitem (3); and
any comments or information received or provided as mentioned in paragraph 29(7)(a) and (b) relating to the approach to be used for assessment of the relevant impacts of the action; and
any information included in the referral of the proposal to take the action relating to the approach to be used for assessment of the relevant impacts of the action; and

any other information, or any comments, relating to the approach to be used for assessment of the relevant impacts of the action received (whether before or after the commencement day) in response to an invitation made before the commencement day under section 74 of the main Act.

Subsections 82(1) and (4) of the main Act apply in relation to the Minister’s decision under subitem (2), as if references in those provisions to controlling provisions were references to provisions of sections 24D and 24E of the main Act as amended by Part 1 of this Schedule.
Within 10 business days after making a decision under subitem (2), the Minister must:
give written notice of the decision to the person proposing to take the action; and
publish notice of the decision in accordance with any regulations made for the purposes of paragraph 91(1)(b) of the main Act.

The Minister must give reasons for the decision to the person proposing to take the action if the person makes a written request, within 28 days of being given the notice, that the Minister do so. The Minister must do so as soon as practicable, and in any case, within 28 days of receiving the request.

(9) The main Act has effect, after the Minister makes a decision under subitem (2) (the new assessment approach decision), as if the decision mentioned in paragraph (1)(b) (the original assessment approach decision) were varied to give effect to the new assessment approach decision.
The validity of the original assessment approach decision, and any other decision made under Part 7, 8 or 9 of the main Act before the Minister made the new assessment approach decision:
is not affected by the making of the new assessment approach decision; and
cannot be revoked, varied, suspended, challenged, reviewed, set aside or called in question because of, or for reasons relating to:
the making of the new assessment approach decision; or
the variation of the original assessment approach decision as described in subitem (9).

Anything done by the Minister under this item is not invalid merely because it was not done within the period required by this item. However, this does not reduce or remove an obligation under this item to do a thing within a particular period.

The Minister may, by legislative instrument, make rules prescribing matters of a transitional nature (including prescribing any saving or application provisions) relating to the amendments or repeals made by Part 1 of this Schedule.

Rules made before the end of the period of 6 months starting on the commencement day may provide that provisions of this Part have effect with any modifications prescribed by the rules. The provisions then have effect as if they were so modified.
To avoid doubt, the rules may not do the following:
create an offence or civil penalty;
provide powers of:
arrest or detention; or
entry, search or seizure;
impose a tax;
set an amount to be appropriated from the Consolidated Revenue Fund under an appropriation in this Schedule or the main Act;
directly amend the text of this Schedule or the main Act.
This Schedule (other than subitem (3)) does not limit the rules that may be made under this item.
